description: Neko runs a full, real Firefox inside the container and streams it to your browser over WebRTC — not VNC. Because WebRTC is built for real-time video over lossy/jittery connections (adaptive bitrate, UDP transport, automatic reconnect), it holds up far better on flaky remote links than VNC/RFB-based browser containers do. Multiple people can also join the same session together (with chat) if you want to co-browse.

env.description: Must exactly match the UDP port range published below — WebRTC needs the host and container port numbers to be identical, not just mapped
env.label: NEKO_WEBRTC_EPR
env.name: NEKO_WEBRTC_EPR

env.description: Your home server's public/reachable IP, needed for WebRTC to work when connecting from outside your LAN. Leave blank to let Neko auto-detect it via STUN (works for most setups); set it explicitly if auto-detection picks the wrong address or you're behind CGNAT with a port-forwarded router.
env.label: NEKO_WEBRTC_NAT1TO1
env.name: NEKO_WEBRTC_NAT1TO1

name: neko-firefox
note: The UDP port range must stay unmapped (host port == container port) for WebRTC to work — don't remap it. For a smoother experience with several tabs open, increase this container's Shared Memory Size (default 64MB) under Portainer's Advanced container settings, similar to how Chromium/Firefox need extra /dev/shm on any Docker host. If you're behind a router (not just accessing over VPN/LAN), you'll also need to forward the WebRTC UDP port range to this host.
title: Neko (Firefox)
